lines.x: Brazil's central bank unanimously kept the Selic rate at 13.75% in November, pausing its rate-cut cycle due to rising uncertainty and inflation expectations.
Energy stocks including Petrobras, YPF, and Ecopetrol fell on November 4, alongside the USO oil fund, as market participants reacted to expectations of an end to the conflict in Iran.
The Brazilian Ibovespa index fell 0.82% to 166,191 points, pressured by fiscal uncertainty and a broader risk-off sentiment in Wall Street.
Brent and WTI crude oil futures declined, trading near four-week lows following peace negotiations involving Ukraine and Iran, after initially opening higher.
